cards.title: Lower-left anchored rectangle packing constant
cards.formal: Determine the universal lower-left anchored rectangle packing constant \(\alpha\) to absolute error at most \(1/100\). For each finite point set \(P\subseteq[0,1)^2\) containing \((0,0)\), let \(A(P)\) be the supremum of the total area of all valid packings of one positive-area axis-aligned rectangle per point, each anchored at that point as its lower-left corner and contained in the unit square. Rectangles must have disjoint interiors. Define \(\alpha=\inf_{P\subseteq[0,1)^2,\;P\text{ finite},\;(0,0)\in P}A(P)\). Area is measured as a fraction of the unit square, so the tolerance is one percentage point of its area.
cards.why: The question asks how much area arbitrary anchors inevitably permit one to occupy. Its mathematical interest comes from the universal guarantee over every finite configuration, including degeneracies, rather than the optimal value of one instance. The half-area conjecture would identify the extremal value, while rigorous estimates of the constant quantify the remaining gap.
cards.status_note: The checked 2021 primary paper and 2023 dissertation leave Freedman’s exact conjecture open and give the interval 0.39 to 0.5 for the associated universal coverage constant. The 2013 proof announcement was explicitly withdrawn. Bounded later-work checks through 2026-09-15 found no verified resolution at the stated precision; this is not an exhaustive certification of all subsequent literature.

progress.text: Freedman poses the half-coverage question, as documented in the checked 2021 paper’s introduction and its reference to Tutte’s collection of unsolved problems.
The authors withdraw the announced existential proof because of an error in Claim 5.

Damerius, Kaaser, Kling and Schneider publish a 39 percent coverage guarantee and a below-43.3-percent limitation for their studied greedy algorithm. The half-coverage conjecture remains a separate general question.
Nölke’s dissertation, defended on 21 February 2023, retains the open conjecture and the 0.39 universal guarantee in its introduction and Chapter 3.

importance.reason: A longstanding geometric extremal problem whose elementary input model hides a large unresolved gap between universal coverage guarantees. It links continuous packing choices with arbitrary finite point configurations, and the demonstrated limitation of the familiar greedy algorithm separates general existence from that algorithm’s performance.

sentences: The target is the worst possible optimal coverage by rectangles anchored at their lower-left corners at arbitrary points of the unit square.
Every finite point set must include the origin, and each point receives a positive-area rectangle with no interior overlap.
The numerical answer must locate the universal coverage constant within one percentage point, with a complete Lean proof.
Freedman’s exact half-coverage conjecture remains the source question and is stronger than satisfying this approximation criterion.
The checked universal bounds are 39 and 50 percent, while the smaller upper bound in the 2021 paper concerns only its particular greedy algorithm.

cards.definitions: Write \(p=(x_p,y_p)\). A valid packing chooses real coordinates \(u_p,v_p\) satisfying \(x_p<u_p\le1\) and \(y_p<v_p\le1\) for every \(p\in P\), and uses \(R_p=[x_p,u_p)\times[y_p,v_p)\). For distinct points \(p,q\), the open sets \((x_p,u_p)\times(y_p,v_p)\) and \((x_q,u_q)\times(y_q,v_q)\) must be disjoint; boundaries may touch. Its total area is \(\sum_{p\in P}(u_p-x_p)(v_p-y_p)\). All points are distinct, their number is arbitrary, and coordinates may be any real numbers in the stated domain. Points may share an x-coordinate or y-coordinate; there is no general-position assumption. The origin is mandatory. The other three corners of a rectangle need not belong to \(P\). Every point anchors exactly one positive-area rectangle, and no rotations, other anchor corners, squares-only restriction, or overlaps of positive area are permitted. Valid packings exist for every such finite set, and their areas are bounded by one. Thus \(A(P)\) and \(\alpha\) are well-defined real suprema and infima. No optimum-attaining point set or packing is demanded by the definitions. There is no computational running-time requirement and no rational-coordinate or finite-precision restriction.
cards.answer_criterion: Supply an unambiguous real value \(a\) and a complete mathematically correct proof checked in Lean that \(|a-\alpha|\le1/100\), with the quantifiers, positivity and boundary conventions above. Equivalently, certify an interval \([L,U]\) containing \(\alpha\) with \(U-L\le1/50\) and take its midpoint. A lower bound \(L\) must hold for every finite allowed point set through its packing supremum; an upper bound \(U\) must bound the infimum over all allowed point sets, allowing a sequence of sets approaching the bound. A value of \(A(P)\) for one selected instance, an uncertified experiment, or only a performance guarantee for a particular algorithm is insufficient. Exact determination is welcome but not required. This numerical benchmark does not claim that a one-percentage-point approximation proves or refutes the exact half-coverage conjecture.

context_blocks.text: Freedman’s original conjecture asks whether every permitted point set admits a packing covering at least \(1/2\) of the square. The ICALP 2021 source states this in its introduction and calls for algorithms reaching that guarantee in its conclusion. This card follows the authorized numerical formulation of extremal targets: it asks for the underlying universal coverage constant, retaining the exact conjecture here as the source question. The numerical acceptance criterion is a broadening, not a claim of logical equivalence to proving the conjecture.

The checked 2021 paper establishes a universal coverage guarantee of \(0.39\), while its introductory extremal comparison gives \(\alpha\le1/2\). Consequently the checked bounds are \(0.39\le\alpha\le0.5\). This interval is wider than the benchmark’s permitted \(1/50\) certified interval.

The same paper exhibits inputs on which its studied greedy packing algorithm covers less than \(0.433\). That is an upper bound on this particular algorithm’s worst-case guarantee. It is not an upper bound of \(0.433\) on the optimum packing constant \(\alpha\), and it does not refute Freedman’s conjecture.

A 2013 preprint announcing a proof was withdrawn on 28 April 2014 because its authors found a bug in Claim 5. Its unchanged abstract must be read together with the withdrawal notice; it is not a verified resolution.

Nölke’s 2023 dissertation still records the half-coverage conjecture as open and cites 0.39 as the best known universal guarantee. Its other anchored-packing variants have different allowed anchor positions and do not automatically settle the lower-left problem.

methodology: Detailed cards have individually written statements, context, significance, and documented results. Source notes are unfinished research records and do not yet meet that standard. The legacy index is retained for traceability.
Open in the source means open at the date of that source. The build date, 10 September 2026, does not establish current open status. Old excerpts may omit conditions or subsequent results.

Selection considers model power, necessary resources, sharp bounds, structural characterizations, explicit constructions, and minimal assumptions. Source notes use a heuristic screen; detailed cards give an individual explanation.

The earlier automatic paper screen allowed at most one new card per paper title and rejected identical formulations and close duplicates within a source. Approved textbook and survey imports retain multiple distinct questions per publication. Confirmed overlaps supplement existing cards; collection-wide semantic deduplication remains incomplete.

Short quotations retain the source language. Later related literature, where listed, is a research aid rather than evidence of resolution. Personal notes and saved cards are stored locally in your browser.

Textbook and survey questions are dated paraphrases; source locations, conjectures, research directions and caveats are preserved on the problem cards. These annotations do not establish current open status or change a later card review. New source drafts remain unassessed for importance. The reader contains the imported questions and external bibliographic references only; source files are not bundled.

Selection groups follow the agreed 10 large and 25 small categories. Our primary goal is a benchmark of 500 problems. Top 100 is a priority subset of those same 500, with secondary editorial attention. Both use the same category order and the same ranking within each category. The existing Top 1000 view is not an active benchmark goal. The respective prefixes are 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 problems per large/small category. The legacy Top 1000 view has 1000 assigned places and 0 reserved places. Each card records its category explicitly. These counts describe saved candidates; classification does not verify a statement or its current open status. Inactive records are archived outside the catalogue, exports and editorial work. Their content, stable IDs and reasons are retained; imports cannot reactivate them. Final quota selection and a comprehensive deduplication audit remain pending.

Importance ordering is an editorial assessment of foundational significance, breadth of consequences, and influence on other questions. Each assessed card gives a reason. The category-wide review also uses shared priority bands for questions of comparable scope; it does not claim that these ties have a scientifically meaningful internal order. Unassessed drafts share a provisional score of 50; their relative order is only an ID tie-break, not an importance judgment. The first 5/2 places in each large/small category are an explicit editorial focus selection balancing importance and topical diversity. Focus ordering does not alter importance scores; remaining candidates use score and ID order. The primary target is 500 problems; Top 100 is its priority subset with secondary editorial attention. Top 100, Top 500 and the legacy Top 1000 view use the first 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 category places respectively, all from the same ranking. Category positions include all candidates and remain fixed when filtering. Publication date, source date, and card detail do not increase importance. Inactive cards, including resolved records, are archived outside the ranking without changing their historical importance score. Importance review does not establish that a saved question is still open.
